questions.q: What distinguishes a "capped/disinflationary" supply model from a "fixed" supply model?
options: They are identical in every way
A capped model has a max supply but mints toward it gradually over time; a fixed model has the entire supply determined at genesis
A capped model has no maximum; a fixed model always has one
A fixed model mints new tokens forever
questions.explain: Fixed supply is set entirely at genesis with no further minting. Capped/disinflationary supply has a ceiling but reaches it gradually through ongoing emissions.

questions.q: Given max supply 1,000,000,000, total supply 600,000,000, and locked/vesting/treasury holdings of 250,000,000, what is the circulating supply?
Why can a market cap calculated from total supply (instead of circulating supply) be misleading?
options: It overstates how much of the token is actually liquid and tradeable right now
Total supply is always smaller than circulating supply
It has no effect -- the two numbers are always identical
Total supply excludes locked tokens, so it understates market cap
questions.explain: Total supply includes locked, vesting, and treasury-held tokens that aren't actually on the market, so using it inflates the apparent market cap.

questions.q: A token mints 20,000,000 tokens in staking emissions and burns 25,000,000 tokens from transaction fees in one year. What is the net supply change?
options: 0 -- emissions and burns always cancel out
questions.explain: net_supply_change = emissions_minted - tokens_burned = 20,000,000 - 25,000,000 = -5,000,000, a net-deflationary year.

questions.q: Can a token have a capped max supply and still be net-deflationary before reaching that cap?
options: No -- capped supply and deflationary supply are mutually exclusive by definition
Yes -- a burn mechanism can remove more tokens than are currently being minted, even while the cap hasn't been reached
No -- burns are only possible on uncapped tokens
Yes, but only if the protocol stops minting entirely
questions.explain: The lesson notes these models aren't mutually exclusive: a capped-supply token with a strong enough burn mechanism can have negative net inflation even before hitting its cap.
